title: Tenant boundary proctoring protocol and locality retention (draft)
summary: Working draft of an operator-focused protocol for validating tenant region pins ("proctoring") and a compact retention policy that balances auditability and storage cost. Includes a lightweight canary plan, operator run steps, evidence formats, and a customer-facing communication template for pinging/retention changes.
audience: SRE/oncall operators, privacy/legal reviewers, solutions engineers prepping customer onboarding for region-bound deployments.
problem_statement: We need an operationally simple, auditable procedure to verify that a tenant that requests/has been assigned a region pin is actually anchored in the expected locality and to manage minimum retention of proof artifacts. Current pin evidence artifacts are inconsistent and expensive to retain long-term; we need a compact, reproducible protocol that operators can run during onboarding and periodic audits.
assumptions: 1) Underlying routing can assert region at request time and emit region headers. 2) Customers will accept short-lived cryptographic evidence (hashes/timestamped receipts) instead of full logs for routine audits. 3) Legal may require raw logs for subpoenas but not for ongoing SLA validation. 4) We have access to benign geo-anchoring sources (edge zone IDs, cloud region metadata, TLS termination locations).
proctoring_protocol_steps:
Step 0 - Scope: confirm tenant's contract pin (country/region) and which endpoints must be enforced.
Step 1 - Baseline capture: from operator console, trigger a controlled batch of requests (20 small sample requests) from tenant account to the pinned route via the normal ingress path. Capture the following: timestamp, request id, observed region header, edge zone id, and upstream egress IP.
Step 2 - Evidence signing: for each captured sample, compute SHA256 over (timestamp|request id|edge zone id|observed-region) and submit that digest to the private evidence store; create an HMAC with the operator key and store the HMAC alongside.
Step 3 - Cross-check: compare observed-region vs. tenant-declared region and cloud region metadata; if mismatch > 10% of samples, escalate to oncall and open JIRA with tag RESIDENCY-INVEST.
Step 4 - Compact retention: retain raw samples for 14 days; retain signed digests + HMACs + operator note for 2 years (single compact file per audit run).
Step 5 - Subjective verification: for high-risk customers, request a biz-contact confirmation (email template in "customer_comm_template") and perform a second proctoring run from an alternate edge zone.
Step 6 - Audit delivery: produce the compact evidence bundle (zip) containing digests, HMAC metadata, operator notes, and canonical provenance statement. For legal requests, provide instructions to escalate to security/legal for raw log extraction.
operator_steps:
Checklist for the oncall/operator (short):
- Verify tenant pin contract and current pin state in tenant metadata.
- Run 'proctor-sample' job from console (UI button or CLI).
- Wait for job completion; review sample hit-rate and region header distribution.
- Generate digest bundle and save to evidence store; attach to tenant case.
- If mismatches detected, set tenant to 'monitoring' mode and notify Solutions Eng + Legal.
- Close run with summary note and tags: pin-audit, tenant-<id>, region-<code>.
telemetry_signals:
Primary signals to populate dashboards and alerting:
- region-header-consistency (percentage per-run)
- proctoring-failure-rate (runs with >10% mismatch)
- compact-evidence-creation-latency
- evidence-store-retention-counts by tenant
- operator-escalation-counts and time-to-ack
Implementation note: add a boolean flag in the trace/span (residency.proctored=true) and surface in per-tenant timeline.
canary_plan:
Goal: validate protocol and retention policy with three customers of varying risk profile: small SMB (low risk), mid-market (medium risk), regulated-pilot (high risk).
Phase A (non-intrusive): run proctoring with daily sample job for 7 days, no customer notification. If any run exceeds 10% mismatch, pause and notify customer.
Phase B (engage): run enhanced proctoring (alternate-edge) and send customer-facing note with draft evidence bundle.
Phase C (opt-in full): if customer agrees, enable scheduled monthly proctoring and include compact evidence on request.
Metrics to track: false-positive mismatches, operator time per-run, compact bundle size, legal requests triggered.
customer_comm_template:
Subject: Short note about region pin verification
Hi <Customer Contact>,
We perform periodic checks to ensure region pin enforcement is operating as contracted. We ran a brief verification on <date> that produced a compact, signed evidence bundle. The bundle contains digests and operator notes (no raw customer data). If you would like the full logs for long-term audit, we can arrange through your compliance lead.
Best,
Redwood Private Operations
retention_compact_spec:
Compact bundle contents:
- manifest.json (list of sample digests, timestamps, edge zone ids)
- signed-digests.sha256 (line-delimited digest + operator id + run-id)
- hmac-metadata.txt (hmac key id, algorithm, signature)
- operator-note.md (free text, why run, anomalies)
Storage rules: keep compact bundles for 2 years; keep raw request logs for 14 days unless legal hold. Cost estimate: ~12 KB per sample digest; ~240 KB per 20-sample run per tenant.
Retention exceptions: customers that contract raw-log archival will have separate storage invoices and longer retention handled by FinOps.
handoff_templates:
Operator -> SRE escalation: short template to create an incident ticket.
Title: Residency mismatch for tenant <id> - run <run-id>
Body: summary, observed-region distribution, manifest link, recommended next action (monitor / immediate rollback / legal contact).
Customer-facing compliance handoff: attach compact bundle and a one-paragraph explanation of what the evidence contains.
open_questions: Do legal/contract agree that signed digests + HMACs are sufficient for routine audits?
Which key management lifecycle do we use for HMAC operator keys (rotation cadence)?
Is 14-day raw-log retention acceptable for incident investigation (vs 30/90)?
How do we surface compact-bundle availability in the Console UI for Solutions Eng?
